target.title: feat: Auto-generate session titles from first user message
target.body:
## Summary

Adds title-based session naming similar to ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude. After the first reply in a new session, an LLM call generates a concise 3-6 word title (e.g. "Python Array Sorting Help") and stores it as `displayName`, which is what `deriveSessionTitle` returns.

This replaces the current behavior of just truncating the first user message at 60 characters.

## Changes

- **`auto-session-title.ts`** — New module with title generation + persistence logic
  - Uses the existing `generateConversationLabel` function (already in codebase but not wired into main flow)
  - Deduplication guard prevents concurrent title requests per session
  - Guards against session rotation and post-first-turn false positives
  - Respects existing explicit names (label, displayName, subject, origin.label)

- **`agent-runner.ts`** — Fire-and-forget hook after the first reply
  - Runs in the background, never blocks the reply path
  - Only triggers for new sessions with non-command user messages
  - Checks `session.autoTitle` config (default: true)

- **`types.base.ts`** — Added `session.autoTitle?: boolean` config option

- **`schema.labels.ts`** — Added schema label for the new config option

- **`auto-session-title.test.ts`** — Unit tests for candidacy checks

## Config

```yaml
session:
  autoTitle: true  # default, set false to disable
```

## How it works

1. User sends first message in a new session
2. Agent generates a reply (as normal)
3. **After** the reply is sent, a background LLM call generates a title from the user message
4. Title is persisted as `displayName` on the session entry
5. `deriveSessionTitle` returns the AI-generated title instead of raw first-message truncation

The entire title generation is fire-and-forget — it never adds latency to the reply path.
